topic: Theme 3: Communication and the World Around Us
subject: french

moments.title: Onesime Reclus coins 'francophonie'
moments.body: The geographer Reclus introduces the term to describe the community of French speakers worldwide.
moments.takeaway: The concept of a francophone community predates institutional structures.

moments.title: ACCT founded
moments.body: The Agence de cooperation culturelle et technique (later OIF) is founded as the institutional core of la Francophonie.
moments.takeaway: International francophone institutions emerged with decolonisation.

moments.title: African demographic centre
moments.body:
Projections suggest the majority of French speakers will live in Africa by 2050.

DR Congo and other states with French as official or working language drive the shift.
moments.takeaway: The geography of major world languages is being reshaped by African demography.

now.title: Francophonie today
now.body: OIF includes 88 states and governments. Many use French as a second language alongside others; education systems remain central to its spread.
now.open_questions: How does African francophone literature and media reshape the language? What role will French play alongside English and Mandarin globally?

reflection: The future of a language often depends on demographic trends well outside the country whose name it bears.
